newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi acquires Beirut bank.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi acquires Beirut bank.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque Audi announced on Thursday the acquisition of Credit Commercial du Moyen-Orient (CCMO), a medium-size Beirut bank.
A statement by Banque Audi Chairman Georges Audi said it had acquired all shares in CCMO and the two banks would be fully merged.
It called CCMO "a well-established national bank" with eight branches and "excellent financial standing."
CCMO's assets of 340 billion Lebanese pounds ($221 million) at the end of 1996 comprised a 0.85 percent market share, the statement said.
The acquisition "is mainly driven by the prevailing needs to reinforce and consolidate the national banking structures in view of the regional and international challenges lying ahead," it said.

Highlights of CCMOs financial standing at end 1996 were 65.2 percent liquidity, a 14.1 percent capital adequacy ratio, and a return on shareholders' equity of 23.5 percent. In the first half of 1997 assets rose 14.7 percent to 390 billion pounds and deposits reached 330 billion, the statement said.
